title: Unread only is on by default and is remembered for the user, any browser
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner/Admin user.
  • 3 notifications addressed to you, from notes a second user wrote on a work order, with a mix of read and unread.
  • A second user account and a second browser/device.
custom_steps:
1. Open the inbox for the first time and read the Unread only filter state.
  2. Turn Unread only off, reload the page, and confirm it stays off for you.
  3. Sign in as a different user on the same browser and check their Unread only default.
  4. Confirm that on release the remembered choice starts from default (old shared setting ignored).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • An Unread only filter narrows the list to unread notifications, and it is on when you first open the inbox.
  • The Unread only setting is remembered for that USER across page loads until they change it - not for the browser, so on a shared terminal one person's choice does not decide what the next person sees.
  • On release every user starts from the default again (anything stored under the old shared key is ignored); re-flipping it stores it against you.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10244 (S1, Work the Notifications inbox); Notifications Update v1 PRD (Confluence 817463297), S1; design boards InboxAfter/Main; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R9: “An Unread only filter narrows the list to unread notifications.”
  • S1-R10: “The Unread only filter is on when the user first opens the inbox.”
  • S1-R11: “The Unread only setting is remembered for that USER across page loads until they change it. It is not remembered for the browser: a shared shop terminal must not let one person's choice decide what the next person sees.”
  • S1-R17: “On release, every user starts from the default again: the remembered Unread only choice is now held per person rather than per browser, so anything stored under the old shared key is ignored. Nobody loses anything but a toggle position, and re-flipping it stores it against them.”

Last checked against build v26.40.7-7ffda69 on 10/5/2026.
